jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.description_html:
Prizeout is a leading NYC-based fintech transforming how people interact with their money by turning everyday transactions into rewarding, value-driven moments. We sit at the intersection of payments, rewards, and loyalty, empowering financial institutions to build deeper connections with their users. We're redefining how people engage with their money through smarter, data-driven rewards. 

We're looking for curious, driven people who are energized by building relationships from scratch and want to grow with a team that's scaling fast. We keep the user at the center of every decision and we value humility, curiosity, and ownership.

About This Role

    As an Account Executive at Prizeout, you'll own credit union deals from first touch to signed partnership. You'll find the right institutions, build a relationship, and then carry those relationships all the way from discovery through demos, stakeholder buy-in, and close. 

    Cold outreach is the foundation of the job. Our buyers are relationship-driven and our sales cycles are long, so the people who win here are the ones prospects actually want to keep in touch with. 

    You'll work closely with senior team members. You’ll get coaching and have support for the deals that need air cover, but the pipeline is yours to build and move.

What You'll Do

  • Own a book of credit union prospects end to end (from cold outreach through close)
  • Prospect relentlessly: cold calls, cold email, LinkedIn, and everything in between
  • Research and build target account lists, identifying the right executives and decision-makers at each institution
  • Run discovery calls and customized product demos
  • Manage deals through long sales cycles, keeping momentum toward next steps
  • Represent Prizeout at industry conferences and events 
  • Own your forecast and keep the CRM clean
  • Test and iterate on messaging, sequences, and outreach channels

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years in an SDR, BDR, or early-stage sales role (experience in a closing role preferred)

  • Proven ability to cold outreach and get meetings booked is required

  • Genuinely personable and comfortable striking up a conversation, in person or zoom

  • Evidence you can carry a deal past the first meeting

  • Persistent and resilient, comfortable with long sales cycles and hearing "not right now"

  • Organized and self-directed, able to work a pipeline without being managed day to day

  • Coachable and hungry to grow into a senior closing role

  • Experience selling into financial institutions, credit unions, or fintech is a plus

How You'll Be Paid

    We built this plan to reward people who beat their number, not just hit it.

  • Competitive Salary (expected range is $90,000-$115,000)

  • Competitive uncapped commission structure

  • Stock Options

Please Note:

  • Must be able to work 5 days/week in our NYC office.

  • Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. indefinitely. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

 

 

Prizeout is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.title: In-House Corporate Counsel
jobs.description_html:

We're seeking passionate individuals to drive our mission forward and transform the landscape of advertising and financial technology. We have built a team that values humility and innovation and we believe that embracing challenges makes us better. We hire people we trust, who will live these values and who are able to find a way to navigate through obstacles, embody an entrepreneurial spirit, and maintain a spirit of optimism. 

About This Role

    We’re looking for an experienced attorney to lead and guide on all legal matters across corporate governance, commercial, risk and compliance matters.  You’ll be a member of our dynamic operations team and report to our VP Strategic Finance and Rev Ops, managing all legal matters and driving our commercial contracting process. What You'll Do

  • Provide legal advice and guidance on corporate governance, contractual matters and regulatory compliance; Ensure compliance with relevant regulations and laws

  • Review, draft, and negotiate contracts, agreements, and legal documents with clients, internal employees, vendors, and other parties

  • Assist with corporate transactions, including fundraising, mergers and acquisitions, and strategic partnerships

  • Counsel Prizeout’s product team on a range of issues including data and privacy compliance, commercial contracts, terms and conditions, privacy policies, consumer and financial regulatory compliance, go-to-market strategy, risk and marketing

  • Oversee various legal aspects of corporate governance, including board and shareholder matters, agendas, minutes, consents and resolutions, as well as equity compensation matters, intellectual property protection, and data and privacy law compliance

  • Collaborate with and manage outside counsel on specialized legal matters, such as intellectual property, human resources and employment matters

  • Draft and update template agreements and corporate documents, corporate and information security policies and procedures

  • Represent the company in legal proceedings, negotiations, and meetings with external parties

  • Maintain organized and up-to-date records of all legal records, documents and correspondence, including enhancing the legal team’s processes and compliance frameworks

What We're Looking For

  • JD from a top law school and active member of the NY State Bar in good standing

  • 3-7 years of experience with a strong primary background in commercial / technology transactions with secondary experience in privacy law; Fintech experience is a plus

  • Corporate law, contract negotiation, and regulatory compliance is also preferable

  • Proven ability to build and maintain positive relationships with internal teams, external clients, and outside counsel

  • Expertise in negotiating, drafting, and modifying key terms of strategic commercial agreements

  • Practical, solution-oriented legal approach with a talent for identifying creative and effective solutions to business challenges

  • Ability to communicate complex legal concepts effectively to non-legal stakeholders

  • Excellent ability to operate and communicate remotely

  • Exceptional judgment, responsiveness and the ability to work independently, prioritizing tasks and meeting tight deadlines with minimal supervision

  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced, collaborative, and high-growth environment

Please Note

  • This role can be completed remotely (CST/EST hours), with travel to the NYC office for training and periodic meetings.

jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a Legal Lead to raise the legal bar at Payflip. You'll be our first legal hire and the in-house point of contact for every product- and client-related legal question, from social and tax law to social security. Not only at the finish line, but at the table from the very start.

🌟 Where you fit in

Payflip started as a flexible rewards tool. Today, we're becoming Belgium's salary super app: one platform where companies and people manage their salaries and benefits. Every one of those products sits directly on top of Belgian tax and social (security) law. Each benefit comes with its own RSZ rules, fiscal treatment and joint committee constraints, and getting it wrong has real financial consequences for employers and employees.

That's why legal questions come in daily: from prospects, from clients and from our own product team. Today, they land with a bunch of different people across the company. As we grow, we want one person who owns legal quality.

You'll work closely with our Sales, Customer Success, Service and Support teams, who come to you with the hard questions, and with our product squads, who build with you. As our first legal hire, you won't have a legal team around you, but you'll have plenty of salary-savvy colleagues to spar with.

🧑‍💻 Your mission

Raise the quality and consistency of Payflip's legal answers. Concretely, your job is fourfold:

Own the hard questions. When a lead or client asks a legal question that our commercial or service teams can't answer, it lands with you. You come back with a clear position and a risk assessment, not an "it depends".

Sit at the product table, from the start. You're the legal point of contact for our product team, both proactively and reactively. You don't just double-check what product has already decided: you help shape it. Say a large prospect wants to put a special premium into their flex plan. Who is entitled to it? How is it calculated? What changes with someone's working regime, and what happens at exit? You map that out before we start building, and you pressure-test features, flows, calculations and product copy against HR, tax and social security law before they ship.

Build Payflip's legal brain. You build and own our internal, AI-fuelled legal database: current, structured and usable by non-lawyers. The goal: Payflip AI answers most recurring legal questions correctly, so your time goes to the questions that really need you.

Own the relationship with our external law firms. You filter, frame and escalate the questions that truly need outside counsel, and translate the answers back into clear internal guidance.

The tricky part? Bringing together what the rule says, what the market does, what the client expects and how Payflip looks at salary, and turning that into one answer a client can act on.

To be clear: this is not a corporate or commercial contracting role, and not an HR (people) role. The focus is substantive HR law (social, tax and social security law) applied to our product and our clients.

After 12 months, we'd love to see:

  • Our internal legal database live and adopted, with Payflip AI answering the majority of recurring legal questions at a 90% accuracy rate

  • Escalated lead and client questions answered within 24 hours, with a clear position and risk assessment

  • All escalations to external law firms routed through you, with one framing, and external legal spend staying flat while we grow

  • A working legal review loop with product: no feature ships with an unresolved legal risk

You would be a good fit with our team if most of this sounds like you:

  • 3-5 years of advisory experience in Belgian HR law. At a law firm, consultancy, social secretariat or a Big 4 employment/reward practice, with a proven track record advising clients on social, tax and social security matters. Now you're ready to move in-house at a scaling SaaS company.

  • Solid, opinionated expertise. You know social law, tax law and social security inside out, and you have a view on how to apply them.

  • Pragmatic, not a rule-keeper. You give a workable answer with a clear risk position. You translate Payflip's stance on salary and market practice into concrete steps for clients, not vague legal summaries. Managing risk shouldn't mean blocking product or commercial decisions.

  • You make legal complexity simple. Clear, actionable answers for non-lawyers are your thing. You're just as comfortable in front of a prospect or client as in a product discussion.

  • Tech-minded. You're comfortable turning legal rules into structured logic, working alongside product and engineering, and using AI and tooling to scale legal work. You'd rather productise knowledge than answer the same question twice.

  • A knowledge builder. You know how to structure and maintain a legal database that others actually use.

  • Sound judgement. You know what really needs external counsel and what doesn't.

  • High ownership and autonomy. You don't need a large legal team or hierarchy around you to operate.

About NeoDay

For decades, loyalty programs meant endless IT projects and ROI "somewhere in year three." We think that's broken, so we're proving the opposite. At NeoDay, we help retailers and consumer brands, from supermarkets and fashion chains to fast food and fuel stations, turn loyalty into a real growth engine. Our platform combines AI-driven personalization, gamification and ready-to-launch apps, so brands like Tesco, Action and La Place can go live in weeks instead of years.

NeoDay is the award-winning loyalty platform. We won Best Retail Loyalty Program Worldwide at the International Loyalty Awards and were named by Forrester among the world's leading loyalty platforms. Everything we build is made in-house in The Netherlands and the Philippines, and we're scaling fast across Europe and beyond.

Your role

A loyalty program isn't won on launch day. It's won in the months after: every new member, every campaign that lands, every euro of uplift on the client's books. When our clients succeed, NeoDay grows with them. You're the one who makes that happen.

As Customer Success Manager, you own a portfolio of our international brands from go-live onwards. You become an extension of their marketing team: the loyalty expert at the table who knows what to launch next, why it will work, and how to prove it did. Strategy, results, and a story your client can take straight to their board. You report to our Head of Customer Success and work hand-in-hand with our Solution Architects, Sales, Product, Data and Support teams.

  • Own your book: Be the go-to partner for a portfolio of international brands, from the loyalty manager running campaigns to the C-suite signing off on budget.

  • Define what winning looks like: Set clear goals and a proper baseline with every client, and turn them into a Success Plan you both steer on.

  • Make value impossible to ignore: Deliver campaign results, impact snapshots and benchmarks that your champions share with their leadership. The kind of numbers that get forwarded to the CEO with "have you seen this?"

  • Lead the strategic conversation: Run QBRs, shape the marketing and campaign calendar, and bring loyalty ideas that grow members, visit frequency and basket size.

  • Grow the program, grow the account: Drive adoption and the growth built into every contract. Spot expansion opportunities early and team up with Sales to land them.

  • Never rely on one champion: Map stakeholders, build relationships across marketing, IT and leadership, and make NeoDay part of how the whole organization works.

  • Be the Voice of the Customer: Bundle client feedback into sharp input for Product and bring the roadmap back to your clients. You know when to say "yes," when to say "not now," and how to say "no" so it still lands well.

  • Raise the bar for Customer Success: Help set the standard for how NeoDay partners with its clients. You bring best practices, sharpen how we work and make excellence the norm in every account.

What you bring

  • Experience: 4–7 years in Customer Success, Account Management or client-side CRM / loyalty marketing, ideally at a SaaS or martech company working with retail or consumer brands.

  • A marketer at heart: You speak the language of CMOs and loyalty managers. Campaigns, segments, member lifecycles and promo calendars are your home turf.

  • Data into stories: Baselines, uplift, retention. You're at home in a dashboard and you know which number matters to the board.

  • Trusted advisor: Confident in front of C-level, honest when expectations need resetting, calm when things get hectic.

  • Commercial instinct: You spot growth opportunities before the client does, and you build the business case that turns them into a yes, together with Sales.

  • Client champion: You genuinely care about your clients' success. You listen closely, act before they have to ask and build relationships that feel like partnerships.

  • Languages: Fluent in written and spoken English. Dutch is a bonus.

What you'll get

  • A competitive base salary plus an OTE component: you grow the accounts, you share in the upside.

  • 25 vacation days (based on a full-time contract).

  • A laptop and phone subscription compensation.

  • An international role with a portfolio of leading brands and real commercial impact.

  • Travel allowance / NS card.

  • Great colleagues, team events, and an informal Brabant-style culture: we perform together and enjoy together!

Why NeoDay?

jobs.description_html:
About Monizze

Monizze is a Belgian HR tech and fintech scale-up of ~150 people, and the challenger in employee benefits and flexible compensation. We issue meal, eco and gift vouchers and help employers build flexible pay packages (cafeteria plan, mobility budget), all on one multi-product platform that handles regulated payments. We move faster than the incumbents, and we're growing fast. 

Our mission: turn complex reward topics into simple, usable solutions, a win-win for workers and employers. 

Your advantages first

💪 Your purchasing power is optimized – the motto is true for clients & employees
🌴 30 days off per year: 20 legal holidays + 6 ADV/RTT + 4 Monidayzz

🏠 Homeworking flexibility with days of remote work and a monthly allowance to make it comfy

🧇 Belgian roots, mindset & attitude: a cool and informal atmosphere – one of the best things since waffles

🧠 Your growth is our growth: unlimited learning opportunities (languages, personal growth, hard skills,...)
👪 Your health and your family's health is covered by our hospitalization insurance
✨ Internal mobility is regularly an option for anyone looking to evolve or change jobs or departments
🏠 Homeworking opportunities and overall flexibility
🧳 A yearly trip with all your colleagues to celebrate our achievements
➕ We do much more for our employees, but we needed space to describe the job! We'd love to tell you about it though, so ask us!

Engineering at Monizze

Our engineering organisation is built around agentic coding : our engineers don’t just write code, they lead their agents. Skills, agents and context files are versioned and reviewed with the code. Our standards and Architecture Decision Records are written for people and agents alike. Engineers join each initiative at discovery, alongside Product and UX, and them own its design, build, testing and after-care. Two engineering teams are each led by an Engineering Manager, who coaches +/-7 engineers, makes sure the quality holds and drives agentic adoption engineer by engineer. The Delivery Manager makes sure that what we commit to ships on time and as pitched. The Lead Architect owns the architecture direction and the ADRs and sets the framework for agentic coding. Principal Engineers act as the referents for each stack. One quality bar applies to everyone: be proud of what you ship, and AI-generated code meets the same standard as any other code.

The role

You make sure Monizze's software evolves in one coherent direction, written down and usable by humans and agents alike.

You lead through influence: you stay hands-on, close to the code and the engineers, and your authority comes from the quality of your decisions, the clarity of the standards and the trust you earn.

What You’ll Do

Keep the architecture coherent across products

  • carry the target architecture (multi-product, shared foundations) and make it understandable to everyone, not only to the people who drew it 

  • own the cross-cutting topics: API contracts, gateway and partner API versioning, orchestration vs. choreography, new service vs. new domain 

  • join discovery when an initiative goes beyond our agreed ecosystem or spans several stacks, so structural choices are known before the pitch 

  • surface structural projects early, and bring "done is done" discipline to migrations: frozen scope, explicit go, a closing criterion 

  • take on critical pieces yourself when complexity or urgency calls for it, including during incidents 

Drive architecture decisions

You turn structural choices into Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), keep that base current with the help of Principal Engineers, and make sure every team and agent follows it. You design how each decision is enforced; Engineering Managers check conformity in their teams. 

  • spot early where a structural choice is needed and propose the decision 

  • maintain two sets of ADRs: a short, curated Target that every new component must follow, and a Baseline for existing code that grows one agreed decision at a time 

  • run the ADR lifecycle, from proposal and review with the relevant engineers to decision and publication , and superseding with a new ADR when a decision changes 

  • attach an enforcement mechanism to every ADR (CI, agent skill or PR review) and have every repo declare which rules apply, so CI and agents load the right ones 

  • build consensus among engineers and, when they can't agree, frame the options for the CTO to decide 

Turn tech watch into decisions

Tech watch means turning what’s relevant into concrete proposals.

  • keep a living tech radar (Adopt / Trial / Assess / Hold), the entry point for any new technology discussion

  • run timeboxed experiments with a clear question: successes become an ADR, a standard or a skill, failures get documented too

  • bring in external experts when useful, and make sure their findings end in a decision, not a report

Lead the shift to agentic coding

Move the team from developers who write code to engineers who lead their agents. You set the direction and the framework; the Principal Engineers build the skills, agents and tooling within it.

  • define and regularly revisit the approach: what agents are used for, how, and with which guardrails on critical code (security, payments, card data) 

  • make the standards agent-ready and sponsor the CI steps and review agents that check PRs against them 

  • make the skills and agents landscape converge (shared vs. repo-specific) without killing bottom-up initiative 

  • drive adoption through demos, pairing and onboarding from day one, and track a few meaningful indicators to adjust the course  

Lead the architecture community

  • run workshops, reviews and decision sessions with Principal Engineers and Software Engineers: the standards are theirs, you make them happen 

  • explain the why behind decisions, not only the what, to Product, leadership and business stakeholders 

  • work closely with the CTO, the Delivery Manager and the Engineering Managers to follow-up on architecture risks, experiments and tech debt

What this role doesn’t hold

  • you don't manage people: coaching and performance sit with the Engineering Managers 

  • you don't own delivery, feature design or product priorities. You review and challenge, you don't take over 

  • you don't have the final say on contested decisions: the CTO arbitrates 

  • you're not a gatekeeper on every PR. Within the standards, engineers decide 

What stays yours: whether structural choices are made before the code, whether disagreements actually get decided, and whether engineers see you as a multiplier, not a bottleneck. 

What we’re looking for

  • You have already held an architecture role, by title or de facto (for example as a startup CTO, or as an engineering manager who also owned the architecture). 

  • You have strong experience in software architecture and system design, ideally on multi-product platforms with shared foundations, API contracts and partner integrations. 

  • You have already led the adoption of agentic coding in a team. You practise it daily and understand context engineering, skills, review loops and their limits. 

  • You read, challenge and write code on our stack (PHP/Laravel, Vue/TypeScript, React Native, relational databases, REST APIs, Docker, message queues). 

  • You have aligned several teams around shared standards without hierarchical authority. 

  • You have recorded decisions in ADRs (or an equivalent) and made standards enforceable through CI, linters and architecture tests. 

  • You have a solid general knowledge of cloud infrastructure, security and CI/CD. Experience as an infrastructure architect is a plus. 

  • Experience with payments or other regulated environments (PCI DSS, ISO 27001) is a plus. 

  • You are fluent in English and in French or Dutch

Your profile

  • Hands-on: you run POCs and spikes regularly, and you take on the critical pieces yourself, whether they are complex or urgent. In a crisis, you're in the room helping to fix it, not watching from the side. 

  • Pragmatic: you balance target vision with legacy reality. 

  • Curious but structured: you separate hype from what's useful and prove it with a timeboxed experiment. 

  • A facilitator: you turn a disagreement into clear options and explain a decision to a non-technical audience. 

  • A multiplier: engineers come to you because it helps them move faster.

Why join Monizze ?

Monizze sits at the intersection of purchasing power, payments, mobility and employee benefits. A Belgian challenger with genuine ambition and the pace to match. You'll shape how a regulated, multi-product platform evolves, and lead a whole engineering team into agentic coding while the practices are still being written. 

Two outcomes are always valid here: change the standard, or follow it. If you want to keep the first possible and the second clear, let's talk.
